## 7a208a91bae09a8b · other · low · not-a-defect

**Fact:** Whether a model switch on a scheduled routine needs a human: DeepBench's fourteen routines can only be re-pinned by an attended session, while Anthropic's scheduled deployments reference an agent whose model and per-run dollar budget are updated through the API, with no attended step.

**Locations:**
- `scripts/sync-routine-models.js:7-9` — "It plans the
// change, builds the body, grades the read-back and records the decision; the one act it cannot
// perform -- the `update` itself -- belongs to an attended session."
- `scripts/sync-routine-models.js:17-18` — "the `Claude_Code_Remote` connector's `update_trigger` REFUSED: "this routine was created via
// http_api, not by an agent. Agents can only update routines they created""
- `docs/runbooks/model-watch-routine.md, Step 5` — "AGT-145 proved a cloud run cannot update a routine (`update_trigger` refuses routines created via http_api), so the manager's record is a `routine-pin-pending` decision per routine, and the next attended session runs AGT-145's `--plan` → `update` → `--verify` → `--record`."
- `https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/scheduled-deployments (retrieved 2026-10-19)` — "A **scheduled deployment** allows an agent to start sessions autonomously, enabling task completion over a predictable cadence. You create and manage deployments with the Deployments API, part of the Claude API. ... Pass the optional `budget` object when you create or update the deployment. ... The deployment copies the cap onto each session it starts, so the budget bounds every run separately rather than acting as a cumulative ceiling across runs"
- `https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/opus-5-5/migration-guide (retrieved 2026-10-19)` — "If you use Claude Managed Agents, no changes beyond updating the model name are required."
- `runner_budget/2026-10 (task_context platform_facts.budget)` — "{"month":"2026-10","month_cap_usd":"100.00","day_default_usd":"5.00","weekly_rest_pct":90,"runner_share_pct":50,"final_day_rest_pct":90}"

**Proposed resolution:** Home stays docs/runbooks/model-watch-routine.md step 5 / AGT-145 unless John funds a change: scheduled deployments bill API dollars under the $100/month runner_budget cap where routines today spend the Max 20x subscription (John 5f638ad8: no plan change). A discovery session (CLAUDE.md pointer) sizes the monthly cost before any build; the spend decision is John's.

**Ruling:** The comparison is real but nothing here is broken. DeepBench's routines can only be re-pinned by an attended session because the connector refuses routines it did not create, and that is the ruled design (AGT-145, model-watch-routine.md step 5), recorded as a routine-pin-pending decision. Anthropic's scheduled deployments would remove the attended step but bill API dollars against the 100-a-month runner_budget cap, where the routines today run on subscription tokens -- a spending question nobody has put to John, not a repair. Confidence is low and the current home works, so: not a defect. (devmanager, 2026-10-19)

## 3e398a3232d98a0d · stale-or-irrelevant · high · ticketed

**Fact:** How `tokens_per_pct` on a `runner_usage_readings` row is calibrated: step 3(c) still instructs each cycle to derive it from the two most recent readings, while the same runbook's SES-128 paragraph rules that window wrong and makes one call the only deriver.

**Locations:**
- `docs/runbooks/runner-cycle.md:1375` — "- **Subscription tokens (the governor that replaced the phantom-dollar wall):**
  read the latest `runner_usage_readings` row (John's typed-in meter percentages).
  (a) `all_models_pct ≥ rest_pct` from `resolve_day_token_cap()` (85; 90 from Thursday 01:00 to the reset) → rest: `did_not_run`, reason "weekly meter at
  N% — resting", END. (b) No reading, or latest older than 48h → today's allowance =
  `stale_fallback_tokens` (3M). (c) Otherwise: calibrate `tokens_per_pct` from the estimated
  tokens logged between the two most recent readings vs. the meter delta (store it on the
  reading row); remaining weekly pool = `(100 − all_models_pct) × tokens_per_pct`; today's
  availability = pool ÷ days left in the meter week; runner allowance = availability ×
  `runner_share_pct` (50%), capped at `runner_day_token_allowance` (10M) until two readings
  exist to calibrate from. Sum today's `est_tokens_dev + est_tokens_qa`; at or over the

  dollar track above works** (register B32, John live 2026-08-20 21:0xZ"
- `docs/runbooks/runner-cycle.md:1399` — "**THE CALIBRATION IS DERIVED BY ONE CALL, NOT BY EACH CYCLE'S ARITHMETIC (`SES-128`,
`v7.0.163`, migration `ses128_reading_slots`).** Step (c) above describes calibrating
`tokens_per_pct` from "the two most recent readings", and **that instruction has never once been
carried out** — measured before this shipped, all eight stored `runner_usage_readings` rows carry
`tokens_per_pct = NULL`, so every allowance this runner has ever computed fell through to the
uncalibrated 10M cap or the 3M stale floor. The reason is not that cycles forgot: **the two most
recent readings are the wrong window.** John's meter is spent by his own manual sessions *and* the
runner, so any window mixing the two yields a rate that is confidently wrong. Run this instead,
before you compute the allowance:"
- `docs/runbooks/runner-cycle.md:1120` — "**Pins (`SES-86` — the queue engine, register B5, `v7.0.140`):** a directive-box line matching
`TICKET-ID — move to N` sets that ticket's `pinned_position = N` (then run the recompute — the
pin takes its absolute slot, everything else renumbers around it); `TICKET-ID — release` clears
it. Latest call wins a collision (`updated_at` breaks the tie in the function); completion or
removal clears the pin automatically inside the recompute. A pin line is consumed as a pin, not
stored as a directive row. All other non-empty directive text in the page becomes a
`runner_directives` row (verbatim). A saved
usage reading (the three meter percentages John types in) becomes a `runner_usage_readings`
row: store the percentages verbatim, compute `est_tokens_since_prev` (sum of cycle token
estimates since the prior reading) and `tokens_per_pct` (that sum ÷ the all-models delta,
only when the delta is positive and the window is runner-only — overnight windows qualify;
otherwise leave it NULL rather than storing a confounded number). Update the
ladder with a before-image first, always. *(Supervised run: if the page is unreachable from
the cloud session, log that in the cycle row and continue — this "

## 43b4da4bdb499bdc · contradiction · high · ticketed

**Fact:** EVERY DECISION WINDOW IS STUCK: sweep_decision_windows() aborts the whole batch on one row, so no window has finalised and no work class has been promoted platform-wide for at least four hours. The abort is backlog_done_requires_verdict() (AGT-166) raising on AGT-281: it cannot be written done over its latest verdict block 38959e02-fdd5-4858-bf19-11fc48fdc5d2 without a ship or ticket-status decision dated at or after it. The hourly pg-cron finaliser runner-window-finaliser hits the identical error on every run — runner_finaliser_runs rows at 07:17, 08:17, 09:17 and 10:17 UTC on 2026-10-19 all read finalized 0, promoted 0, closed 0 with that message — and the tail call in this cycle raised the same error. Because the function is one transaction over all due rows, a single unresolvable ticket blocks every other ticket's window, and nothing surfaces this to John: the failure lives only in runner_finaliser_runs.error, which no briefing section reads.

**Locations:**
- `undefined` — "undefined"
- `undefined` — "undefined"

**Proposed resolution:** Make the sweep per-row fault-tolerant: finalise each due decision in its own subtransaction and return the rows it could not finalise, with their reason, instead of aborting the batch — the same fail-direction heal-engine.js and tripwire-to-backlog.js already keep. Then surface a non-empty skipped list (and any runner_finaliser_runs.error) on the briefing, so a stuck finaliser is visible rather than silent. AGT-281 itself needs a ship or ticket-status decision dated at or after its verdict block, which is a separate, smaller fix.

**Ruling:** reuses AGT-423 (devmanager, 2026-10-19)

**Ticket:** AGT-423

## 715f90e1937d7874 · contradiction · high · ticketed

**Fact:** RENDER BLOCKED AFTER EVERY SHIP: bulletProvenanceFinding (AGT-191) scans title + plain_after + plain_worth for uuids and treats any token not in the cycle's decisionIds set as another cycle's fact, refusing the whole render. A trigger appends each decision handle to plain_worth, and record_ship_decision()'s own summary text ends '... on verdict <verdict id>'. A verdict id is not a decision id, so every ship card that gets a ship decision carries a uuid the guard cannot match, and CLAUDE-STATE.md can never be rendered after the ship card exists. Measured live this cycle: card 9bc17701 (AGT-489, v7.0.865) refused with offending token 9ca61d8d-99f4-4462-bb12-c9ff627b477c, which is this cycle's OWN verdict row. The card's prose as written by the cycle contained no uuid at all.

**Locations:**
- `undefined` — "undefined"
- `undefined` — "undefined"

**Proposed resolution:** Add the cycle's own runner_verdicts ids to the set bulletProvenanceFinding() compares against (alongside decisionIds), so a handle naming this cycle's own verdict is not read as a foreign fact. Do not strip the handle text: it is the reversal trace §19v requires. Guard with a regression test that files a ship card, records a ship decision, and asserts the render succeeds.

**Ruling:** bulletProvenanceFinding (AGT-191) scans a card's title, plain_after and plain_worth for uuids and treats any token outside the cycle's decisionIds set as another cycle's fact, refusing the whole render. A trigger appends each decision handle to plain_worth, and record_ship_decision()'s own summary names the cycle's own runner_verdicts id -- which is not in decisionIds. So the guard fires on the cycle's own provenance and the render is blocked after every ship, which is the opposite of what a provenance guard is for. / Add the cycle's own runner_verdicts ids to the set bulletProvenanceFinding() compares against, alongside decisionIds, so a handle naming this cycle's own verdict is not read as a foreign fact. Prove both directions: a card citing its own verdict handle renders, and a card citing a genuinely foreign uuid is still refused -- otherwise the fix is indistinguishable from switching the guard off. (devmanager, 2026-10-19)

**Ticket:** AGT-518

**Fact:** the full regression run (AGT-391) read this test red

**Locations:**
- `tests/regression/agt-63-prioritizer.test.mjs` — "r.text is not a function"

**Proposed resolution:** repair ticket for the Development Manager

**Ruling:** Verified in the clone this run, not recalled. tests/regression/add-capability.test.mjs (sorted index 141 of 423) assigns globalThis.fetch at module top level in two bare blocks with no try/finally and never restores it; its second stub (lines 148-155) returns {ok:true,status:200,json:async()=>b} -- no text(), no clone(), and ok([]) for any URL it does not match. tests/regression/run-all.js snapshots and restores process.env per test (SES-215) but holds ZERO references to globalThis or global, so a leaked global is never put back. Every later file runs against that stub. The distribution proves it: of 183 suite reds, 182 sit at index >141 and exactly one (SES-352, index 123) at or below it -- 0.7% red before the leak point against 64.8% after. It also explains the two control arms AGT-473 calls impossible: a made-up runner_settings column answering HTTP 200 instead of 400 is that stub, not PostgREST. / Restore globals, not only process.env: have run-all.js capture and restore globalThis.fetch (and any global a test replaces) around every import, on BOTH arms, exactly as SES-215 restores env, and give add-capability.test.mjs a try/finally that puts the real fetch back. Pin it with a negative control in SES-215-env-isolation.js -- a fixture test that leaks a stub must not change the next test's result. Then re-run the full suite and re-triage whatever is still red per ticket on its own evidence; never weaken an assertion, and do not assume an arm is fixed because the count fell. AGT-473's stated lead, transport-watch.js, is NOT the cause: it wraps fetch once, is idempotent, marks itself with a symbol, and its wrapper is what the leaked stub overwrites. (devmanager, 2026-10-19)

**Ticket:** AGT-473

## cf7a07695d79631d · contradiction · high · ticketed

**Fact:** THE DEVELOPMENT MANAGER CAN NEVER MAKE AN ASSIGNMENT STICK WHILE max_lanes IS 1, BECAUSE THE WALL IT CHECKS COUNTS THE CYCLE ASKING. runner_should_boot() is designed to be read BEFORE a cycle opens its runner_cycles row (step 1 of the routine prompt reads it at that point and got live_lanes 0 of 1 twice today). scripts/run-project.js re-reads the same function from INSIDE an open cycle, where live_lanes is at least 1 by construction, so with max_lanes 1 it always resolves lanes_full and refuses: 'the answer says assign, but a wall stands: runner_should_boot(): lanes_full. Exiting 2 -- no claim, nothing written.' Measured twice this session on consecutive cycles of the same chain: cycle 9e0abf5e (the sub-agent itself read lanes_full plus pickable_count 0 and answered action stop) and cycle 6bc9245b (the sub-agent correctly answered action assign for the queue head AGT-490, and the DRIVER refused it on the wall). Step 5(d) saves the cycle each time — a manager that cannot answer never stops the cycle, so the cycle builds the queue's first row itself — but the manager's assignment, its claim and its ledger row are lost on every single cycle, which is the whole of SES-378.

**Locations:**
- `undefined` — "undefined"
- `undefined` — "undefined"

**Proposed resolution:** Exclude the asking cycle from the lane count the driver checks: pass --cycle-id through to the wall read (runner_should_boot() already takes no argument, so give it an optional p_exclude_cycle, or have run-project.js read the lane count with `id <> <cycle-id>`), exactly as the ticket claim re-assertion is holder-guarded. Second, smaller half: pickable_count also reads 0 once the cycle has claimed its own pick at B40 pick time, so the same exclusion belongs there — a pick path that moved on because THIS cycle holds the claim is already handled downstream as pick_source own-claim (AGT-183), and the wall should agree with it. Guard with a regression test that opens a cycle row, claims the queue head under it, and asserts run-project.js still accepts an assign for that head.

**Ruling:** reuses AGT-269 (devmanager, 2026-10-19)

**Ticket:** AGT-269

Then refresh the facts it should have moved: shared/models.js MODELS as the one home (LOG-35a) with STANDARDS section 12's table rewritten to point at it rather than restating ids, and the orchestrator lane re-pinned to claude-opus-5-5 through apply_model_assignment() on a completed model-trial.js run once AGT-286 unblocks the trial. ## 1e8addd3e806044f · other · medium · ticketed

**Fact:** How a new Claude model id is discovered: the model-watch runbook scrapes two documentation pages with a regex and treats an empty file as could-not-read, while Anthropic's Models API returns every available model with its id, token limits, capabilities and line.

**Locations:**
- `docs/runbooks/model-watch-routine.md:60-61` — "curl -sfL https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/release-notes/overview https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/model-deprecations | grep -oE 'claude-[a-z0-9]+(-[0-9]+)+' | sort -u > $S/ids.txt; echo "ids exit ${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
```
NEW = lines of `$S/ids.txt` absent from `select model_id from public.model_catalog`; a non-zero curl exit or an empty file = could-not-read."
- `https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/overview (retrieved 2026-10-19), Using the Models API` — "You can query model capabilities and token limits programmatically with the Models API. The response includes `max_input_tokens`, `max_tokens`, and a `capabilities` object for every available model.

Each model in the response also has a `line` field, which names the model line it belongs to. ... Read `line` instead of inferring it from the model's `id`."

**Proposed resolution:** Home: docs/runbooks/model-watch-routine.md step 1 (the runbook is the source, the routine the copy, ARCHITECTURE section 19v). Replace the page grep with GET /v1/models on the existing key for the id list and created_at, keeping the deprecations-page read for retirement dates, which the Models API does not carry. No completion tokens; whether the list call bills is not stated on the page.

**Ruling:** One mechanism, three visible consequences. docs/runbooks/model-watch-routine.md step 1 discovers new model ids by curling two documentation pages through a regex and treating an empty file as could-not-read, while Anthropic exposes GET /v1/models returning every available model with its id, token limits, capabilities and line. Because discovery is a scrape, the facts downstream of it went stale: I confirmed in this clone that shared/models.js MODELS still pins HAIKU claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 and SONNET claude-sonnet-4-6, and docs/STANDARDS.md section 12 still presents both as the canonical strings to always use, while Anthropic lists both as legacy and Haiku 4.5's retirement floor passed 2026-10-15. The orchestrator lane in runner_model_lanes has read claude-opus-5 since 2026-09-02 with its Opus 5.5 trial still unrun, although Opus 5.5 is the recommended Opus and cheaper at 4/20 against 5/25 per million tokens. / Replace the page grep in model-watch step 1 with GET /v1/models on the existing key, so discovery is an API read with a status rather than a regex over prose, and let that feed public.model_assignments through the trial path (AGT-144/AGT-146). Then refresh the facts it should have moved: shared/models.js MODELS as the one home (LOG-35a) with STANDARDS section 12's table rewritten to point at it rather than restating ids, and the orchestrator lane re-pinned to claude-opus-5-5 through apply_model_assignment() on a completed model-trial.js run once AGT-286 unblocks the trial. The retirement floor that has already passed makes this a live call risk, not housekeeping. (devmanager, 2026-10-19)

Never root-cause without reuse_backlog_id and never cleanup -- the ticket exists, so a second one is refused.

**Ruling:** ai_activity_log.call_facts is the base of the section 19k signature and ai_call_patterns groups on it, so a writer putting a per-call value in there - a latency, a timestamp, any id - gives every call its own signature and the AI Audit By Pattern rollup degenerates to one row per call. **Proposed resolution:** Rule this ticket, and the ruling lands on the ticket: root-cause with reuse_backlog_id = this ticket's own id plus a project HOMES it (general leaves it where it is and is itself the ruling); root-cause with reuse_backlog_id naming another open ticket SUPERSEDES it; not-a-defect CLOSES it with your reason; list parks it when the fitting project's list is locked; escalate with john_call rules when only John can decide. Never root-cause without reuse_backlog_id and never cleanup -- the ticket exists, so a second one is refused.

Found live 2026-07-28 (S-LOG-51-design part 2). Homed, not closed: the defect is real and still unguarded, and nothing on the open board covers it. / Refuse a rename whose target already carries a superseded_by, or append the hop instead of overwriting it, so a term's history reads as a chain. Note for whoever builds it: dev-mgr-findings is capture-only under your 2026-09-29 rule, so this ticket is recorded there and waits for your word before it is built. (devmanager, 2026-10-19)
